title_en: Hua Zhenming v. Sun Haitao and Jilin Xuan Yu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. — dispute over execution objection by the applicant for enforcement

full_text_en:
Hua Zhenming v. Sun Haitao, Jilin City Xuanyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.  

Dispute over Objection to Enforcement by the Applicant for Enforcement  

Ruling Summary  

According to Article 64 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, the judicial personnel shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, examine evidence comprehensively and objectively, base their judgment on the provisions of law, abide by the professional ethics of judges, and use logical reasoning and the ordinary experience of daily life to independently determine whether evidence has probative force and the extent of such force, and shall disclose the reasons and results of such determination.  

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court  
(2013) Min Shen Zi No. 675  

Petitioner for Retrial (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Sun Haitao, male, Han ethnicity, born on June 25, 1967, residing at No. 28-1-10, Fuzhou Street, Longtan District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.  

Agent Ad Litem: Wang Dongmei, lawyer of Jilin Mingda Weiye Law Firm.  

Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Hua Zhenming (formerly known as Hua Yanming), male, Han ethnicity, born on August 1, 1957, residing at No. 50, Youlian Lane, Fengman District, Jilin City, Jilin Province.  

Agent Ad Litem: Wang Wenjun, lawyer of Jilin Beiguo Law Firm.  

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance): Jilin City Xuanyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xuanyu Company). Domicile: No. 268, Jihua Road, Yongji Economic Development Zone, Jilin Province.  

Legal Representative: Chi Tieji, Chairman of the Board of the company.  

The petitioner for retrial, Sun Haitao, filed a petition for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2012) Ji Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 13 rendered by the Jilin Provincial High People's Court in the case of dispute over an objection to enforcement by the applicant for enforcement against the respondents Hua Zhenming and Jilin City Xuanyu Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xuanyu Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to review this case, and the review has now concluded.  

Grounds for the Petition for Retrial Submitted by Sun Haitao:  

(1) The original judgment found that execution was permissible, but there was no evidence of the basic fact that the subject matter of execution actually belonged to the judgment debtor Xuanyu Company. Hua Zhenming merely applied for property preservation during the litigation phase concerning the commercial premises occupied by Sun Haitao.  

(2) Sun Haitao lawfully possessed the disputed commercial premises and should, by analogy, apply the provisions on possession protection in the Property Law, rather than the provisions on preservation and execution in civil proceedings. The premises should not be subject to compulsory enforcement. Hua Zhenming held a contractual claim against Xuanyu Company. Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company signed a commercial housing sales contract on March 2, 2006, paid the full price on the same day, and moved into the premises by the end of 2006, taking possession and use of the commercial premises.  

(3) The original judgment applied the law incorrectly. The original judgment mechanically found that Sun Haitao did not possess the disputed commercial premises, simply based on the fact that Sun Haitao was not present in the disputed premises at the time of preservation. This is a legal joke.  

(4) The original judgment confused legal relationships. At first instance, the focus was on the preservation measures; at second instance, the focus shifted to whether Sun Haitao had acquired the property in good faith, but it never examined whether Hua Zhenming had a right that could prevail over Sun Haitao's right and whether execution could continue. Sun Haitao, as a consumer, lawfully enjoyed a priority right of residence over the disputed commercial premises. As long as it was established that he had not colluded with Xuanyu Company to harm the lawful interests of Hua Zhenming, a creditor of Xuanyu Company, his defense should be upheld, and the claim by Hua Zhenming for permission to execute the disputed commercial premises should be dismissed. Sun Haitao applied for retrial under subparagraphs (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.  

Defense of the Respondent Hua Zhenming:  

The grounds for Sun Haitao's petition for retrial are untenable and should be dismissed.  

The following facts were found and confirmed upon this Court's review:  

With respect to the commercial housing sales contract signed between Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company, in the column for the contracting parties, the buyer was stated as Sun Haitao, with his ID card number written, but the address and telephone contact column was left blank. Article 3, concerning the basic particulars of the purchased commercial housing, stated: "The commercial housing purchased by the buyer (hereinafter referred to as the commercial housing, the floor plan of which is shown in Appendix 1 to this contract, and the house number shall prevail as indicated in Appendix 1) is the [building] [block] 3, Unit 20, No. 6 from the east, commercial premises," with a construction area of 25.11 square meters. Article 4, concerning the pricing method and price, stated: RMB 4,200 per square meter, total amount RMB 105,462. Article 5, concerning area confirmation and handling of area discrepancies, was left blank. Article 6, concerning payment method and time limit, was left blank. Article 7, concerning the buyer's liability for overdue payment, was left blank. Article 8, concerning the delivery period agreement, stated: "The seller shall deliver the commercial housing that meets the following conditions and conforms to the terms of this contract to the buyer for use: 1. The commercial housing has passed acceptance inspection. 2. The commercial housing has passed comprehensive acceptance inspection. 3. The commercial housing has passed phased comprehensive acceptance inspection. 4. The commercial housing has obtained the approval documents for commercial housing delivery and use." This was left blank. Article 9, concerning the seller's liability for overdue delivery, was left blank. Article 10, concerning planning and design changes, was left blank. Article 11, concerning the delivery handover, stated: "After the commercial housing meets the conditions for delivery and use, the seller shall notify the buyer in writing to go through the delivery procedures. At the time of acceptance handover between both parties, the seller shall present the certification documents specified in Article 8 of this contract and sign the house handover form. If the seller fails to present the certification documents or presents incomplete certification documents, the buyer has the right to refuse the handover, and the liability for delayed delivery arising therefrom shall be borne by the seller." This was left blank. Article 12 stated: "The seller guarantees that the sold commercial housing has no disputes over property rights or creditor-debtor disputes. If, due to the seller's reasons, the commercial housing cannot undergo property registration or if creditor-debtor disputes arise, the seller shall bear full responsibility." This was left blank. Article 13, concerning the seller's liability for breach of commitments on decoration and equipment standards, was left blank. Article 14, concerning the seller's commitments on the normal operation of infrastructure and public supporting buildings, was left blank. Article 15, concerning the agreement on property registration, was left blank. Article 16, concerning warranty liability, was left blank. Article 19, concerning whether disputes between the parties would be resolved through arbitration or litigation, was left blank. Article 22, concerning how many copies the contract (including appendices) comprised, was left blank. At the end of the contract, in the buyer's signature column, "Sun Haitao" was written. During questioning by this Court, Sun Haitao stated that his wife had signed on his behalf. The date in the buyer's column was left blank.  

On the receipt submitted by Sun Haitao as proof that he had paid the full price for the commercial premises, the amounts in lowercase and uppercase were inconsistent. The lowercase amount was the contract amount of "105,462" yuan; the uppercase amount was "壹拾万零伍仟" (one hundred thousand and five thousand), without the following "肆佰陆拾贰元整" (four hundred and sixty-two yuan). The columns for finance supervisor, bookkeeper, cashier, reviewer, and handling person on the receipt were all blank. The date of issuance on the receipt was blank. The company seal of Xuanyu Company was not stamped in the "unit seal" column at the lower left corner but in the middle-right part of the receipt.  

During the trial at first instance on the morning of March 15, 2011, Sun Haitao testified that on March 2, 2006, his wife signed the commercial housing sales contract on his behalf; after paying the full amount on the spot, Xuanyu Company immediately handed the keys to the commercial premises to Sun Haitao personally. "I paid the money, and they gave me the keys."  

During the questioning by this Court on the morning of August 16, 2013, at the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province, when asked "Did they give the keys to your wife or to you?", Sun Haitao testified: "They gave them to my wife."  

The third photograph on page 17 of the second-instance case file showed a civil ruling by the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province affixed to the door of the disputed commercial premises, sealing the premises. The photograph was taken at 14:44:27 on October 12, 2007.  

Opinion of this Court:  

The review of this petition for retrial concerns the following issues:  

I. Whether, at the time the people's court took the sealing measure against the disputed commercial premises, Sun Haitao had already taken possession of the disputed commercial premises.  

Based on the facts found by the courts of first and second instance, on October 10, 2007, Hua Zhenming and Xuanyu Company filed a lawsuit with the court due to a contract dispute. The next day, Hua Zhenming applied for property preservation during litigation. On the same day, the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province issued the civil ruling (2007) Ji Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 75-3, sealing 23 residential units, 8 commercial premises, and 12 garages, including the disputed commercial premises (Unit 20, Building 3, No. 6 from the east) located in the Jiangpan Mingyuan Residential Community, Jilin City.  

On October 12, 2007, when the judges of the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province conducted the on-site sealing of the Jiangpan Mingyuan Residential Community, they questioned Dong Shengqiang, the manager of the then property management company of the community, Jilin City Tianci Property Management Co., Ltd., and Xu Menghe, the on-site custodian of the construction unit of the Jiangpan Mingyuan Residential Community. Both persons confirmed that as of October 12, 2007, 24 households in Building 3 of the Jiangpan Mingyuan Residential Community had completed the move-in procedures with Xuanyu Company, and the disputed commercial premises (Unit 20, Building 3, No. 6 from the east) had not been moved into.  

On September 23, 2009, the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province issued the civil ruling (2007) Ji Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 75-5, continuing the sealing of the above properties. On February 5, 2010, the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province rendered the civil judgment (2007) Ji Zhong Min Yi Chu Zi No. 75, ordering Xuanyu Company to pay Hua Zhenming RMB 837,210 plus interest losses. After the judgment took effect, Hua Zhenming applied to the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province for compulsory execution. After the case entered the enforcement phase, Sun Haitao raised an objection on the ground that the disputed commercial premises had been purchased by him.  

The above facts are not only evidenced by Hua Zhenming's application for property preservation during litigation, the civil ruling of the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province, and the records of the judges' questioning, but also by the photograph of the disputed commercial premises taken at 14:44:27 on October 12, 2007. This is sufficient proof. Sun Haitao denied these facts but did not provide any evidence to support his denial; therefore, this Court does not accept his position.  

During the hearing before this Court, Sun Haitao testified that on the very day he signed the contract with Xuanyu Company, i.e., March 2, 2006, Xuanyu Company handed the keys to his wife. However, an examination of the trial record at first instance shows that he testified that Xuanyu Company handed the keys to him personally. Sun Haitao's testimony regarding whether the keys were handed to him personally or to his wife is contradictory. At the time of the trial at first instance, he clearly stated: "I paid the money, and they gave me the keys." Yet at the second instance, his attorney Wang Dongmei stated in her representation that "at the end of 2006, the defendant Xuanyu gave the keys to the appellant [Sun Haitao]." The building containing the disputed commercial premises had not passed completion acceptance in March 2006; water, electricity, and gas were not connected; and up to the present, the building does not have a commercial housing pre-sale permit. Considering that under normal circumstances, when handing over keys, one must prepay water, electricity, and gas fees, and that the keys are handed over by the property management company only after the move-in procedures have been completed, Sun Haitao's testimony that he received the keys on the same day he signed the contract is not only inconsistent with common sense but also self-contradictory. If the keys had indeed been handed over on that day, Sun Haitao should have remembered such a significant event clearly. According to Article 11 of the commercial housing sales contract, the parties must sign a house handover form upon acceptance and handover. However, Sun Haitao did not provide any evidence of the key handover. His attorney Wang Dongmei stated in the representation at second instance: "At the end of 2006, the defendant Xuanyu handed the keys to the appellant." Taking all these factors into consideration, this Court is convinced that Xuanyu Company did not hand over the keys to the disputed commercial premises to Sun Haitao or his wife on March 2, 2006. Since Sun Haitao's claim that Xuanyu Company handed over the keys on the same day the contract was signed cannot be sustained, and since no one had completed the move-in procedures for the disputed commercial premises before October 12, 2007, this Court finds that at the time the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province sealed the disputed commercial premises on October 12, 2007, Sun Haitao and his wife did not have the keys to the disputed commercial premises. In his petition for retrial, Sun Haitao claimed that he moved into the disputed commercial premises at the end of 2006, based on his assertion that he received the keys to the disputed commercial premises on March 2, 2006. Since this assertion cannot be established, there is no basis for his claim, and this Court does not support it. Therefore, it is evident that Sun Haitao's claim that he had already taken possession of the disputed commercial premises at the time of the sealing by the Jilin Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province on October 12, 2007, cannot be sustained. Consequently, the first three grounds raised in Sun Haitao's petition for retrial are all untenable. The precondition for these three grounds is that Sun Haitao had already taken possession of the disputed commercial premises at the time of the sealing by the people's court on October 12, 2007. However, Sun Haitao did not lawfully possess the disputed commercial premises as of that date. Therefore, his argument that this case should apply, by analogy, the provisions on possession protection in the Property Law, rather than the provisions on preservation and execution in civil proceedings, and that the premises should not be subject to compulsory enforcement, is clearly untenable. Sun Haitao claimed in his petition for retrial that the original judgment applied the law incorrectly. He argued that the original judgment mechanically found that Sun Haitao did not possess the disputed commercial premises, simply based on the fact that Sun Haitao was not present in the disputed premises at the time of preservation, and that this was a legal joke. Based on the above reasoning, this ground is also clearly untenable. Furthermore, if Sun Haitao had already occupied the disputed commercial premises at the time of the on-site sealing on October 12, 2006 (note: the text appears to contain a typographical error; it should likely be 2007), Sun Haitao should have raised an objection. However, Sun Haitao did not raise any objection. Sun Haitao defended himself by claiming that he had leased out the premises. This Court finds this doubtful. The building housing the disputed commercial premises was not yet completed; water, electricity, and gas were not connected. Who would have leased the premises? If a lessee had leased it, the lessee would have used it, and the then property management company of the community and the on-site custodian of the construction unit, Xu Menghe, would have known. However, the property management company manager Dong Shengqiang and Xu Menghe confirmed that no one had moved into the disputed commercial premises. Even assuming the lease defense is valid for the sake of argument, since the lessee leased the premises for use, and the on-site sealing status would have persisted for some time, the lessee should have known that the disputed commercial premises had been sealed. Upon learning this, the lessee should have contacted Sun Haitao, and Sun Haitao should have known about the sealing and raised an objection. However, Sun Haitao did not raise an objection. Therefore, this defense of Sun Haitao is untenable. The above reasoning also demonstrates that Sun Haitao's claim that he moved into the disputed commercial premises at the end of 2006 cannot be sustained. When the people's court continued the sealing of the disputed commercial premises on September 23, 2009, if Sun Haitao had already occupied the premises, he should have raised an objection. However, Sun Haitao did not raise an objection at that time either. It was not until Hua Zhenming requested the enforcement of the judgment debtor Xuanyu Company's property and the case entered the enforcement phase that Sun Haitao raised an objection on the ground that the disputed commercial premises had been purchased by him. This is also an important reason supporting this Court's finding.  

II. Whether Sun Haitao had already paid the full price for the disputed commercial premises on March 2, 2006, and whether he enjoyed a "priority right of residence."  

In his petition for retrial, Sun Haitao argued that as a consumer, he lawfully enjoyed a priority right of residence over the disputed commercial premises. As long as it was established that he had not colluded with Xuanyu Company to harm the lawful interests of Hua Zhenming, a creditor of Xuanyu Company, his defense should be upheld, and the claim by Hua Zhenming for permission to execute the disputed commercial premises should be dismissed. This Court finds that this ground is also untenable. The reasons are as follows:  

(A) Sun Haitao did not pay the price of RMB 105,462 for the disputed commercial premises on March 2, 2006. Sun Haitao did not provide any evidence of this during the first instance. During the second instance, he submitted two new pieces of evidence: Evidence 1: five cashier's check stubs, purporting to prove that Sun Haitao withdrew a total of RMB 200,000 in cash from the bank and paid the entire amount to Xuanyu Company on March 2; Evidence 2: a detailed statement of registered capital paid-in and an enterprise legal person business license, intended to corroborate Evidence 1. Hua Zhenming raised the following objections during cross-examination: (1) The two pieces of evidence do not constitute new evidence. (2) They do not demonstrate the purpose of the funds. (3) The subject of the checks was a company, and they should be considered as corporate acts, not acts of Sun Haitao. (4) The withdrawal dates all fell in February 2006, too long before the payment date. This Court finds that Hua Zhenming's objections are valid. The reasons are as follows:  

First, during questioning by this Court, Sun Haitao testified that he "paid the money first, then signed the contract," which is clearly contrary to common sense. Who would pay for a commercial property like this without first signing a contract? The contract price in this case is RMB 105,462. Without a signed contract, how would this specific amount, which includes a precise figure, have been calculated?  

Second, the commercial housing sales contract itself between Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company contains many suspicious points. Firstly, Sun Haitao stated that the signature "Sun Haitao" at the end of the contract was signed by his wife on his behalf. Sun Haitao explained this by saying, "because I had been hospitalized before and was in poor health," and "my handwriting is ugly." When this Court asked, "Did the other party know that you were a married couple?", Sun Haitao answered, "Yes." These responses raise doubts. For a person with full capacity for civil conduct, who was present at the time of signing, to merely write down his own name and the date of signing, is it a valid reason to have his wife sign on his behalf because he was in poor health or his handwriting was ugly? Moreover, if Xuanyu Company knew that Sun Haitao and his wife were a married couple, they could have used the wife's name to purchase the commercial premises. Why take the extra step of using Sun Haitao's name? Under normal circumstances, Xuanyu Company should have had the contracting party, Sun Haitao himself, sign the contract. Only in extremely rare and exceptional circumstances would Xuanyu Company allow Sun Haitao's wife, who was present, to sign on his behalf, and in such a case, a copy of the marriage certificate would have to be provided as evidence. If they did not know the relationship, proving it would require producing the marriage certificate and making a copy. Given these complications, it would have been simpler for Sun Haitao to sign the contract himself, as signing requires minimal effort. Therefore, Sun Haitao's testimony that his wife signed on his behalf is contrary to ordinary life experience. Secondly, the signature "Sun Haitao" at the end of the contract was not followed by the date (year, month, day), which is inconsistent with the usual practice of immediately writing the date after signing a contract and also contradicts ordinary life experience. Thirdly, many important terms of the contract were left blank, such as: (1) payment method and time limit; (2) the buyer's liability for overdue payment; (3) the conditions under which the seller should deliver the commercial premises to the buyer for use, such as whether the premises had passed acceptance inspection; (4) the method of handover between the parties; whether the buyer had the right to refuse handover if the seller failed to present or presented incomplete certification documents; (5) the seller's liability for overdue delivery; and (6) the agreement on property registration. Finally, Article 3 of the contract stipulated that the floor plan of the subject property was to be found in Appendix 1 to this contract, and the house number should be as indicated in Appendix 1. However, the contract did not include "Appendix 1."  

Third, the subject of the checks was not Sun Haitao but a company. The ownership of the funds belonged to the company, not to Sun Haitao. Sun Haitao did not provide any evidence that he had borrowed the funds from that company.

Fourth, the time for withdrawing cash via checks was on February 5, 6, 7, 9, and 10, with a total amount of RMB 200,000. However, Sun Haitao stated that the time for paying the price of the disputed premises was March 2, with a difference of more than 20 days. That is, Sun Haitao kept the RMB 200,000 in cash at home for over 20 days, which is clearly inconsistent with common sense. This is because, was Sun Haitao already negotiating with Xuanyu Company more than 20 days in advance to purchase the disputed premises on March 2? If so, why did he not write a check to withdraw the cash on March 2 itself or a few days before? Or directly endorse the check to Xuanyu Company? If there was no negotiation more than 20 days in advance, then the probative force of the evidence presented by Sun Haitao is very weak, not conforming to the common experience of daily life. Pursuant to Article 64 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, which provides that "judicial personnel shall, in accordance with statutory procedures, comprehensively and objectively examine evidence, follow the provisions of the law, adhere to judges' professional ethics, use logical reasoning and common experience of daily life to independently determine whether evidence has probative force and the degree of probative force, and disclose the reasons and results of such determination," solely on the basis of this evidence, this Court cannot be convinced that this cash was used to pay the price of the disputed premises.

Fifth, Xuanyu Company did not issue a formal invoice, but only a temporary receipt. Xuanyu Company did not have a pre-sale permit for the commercial premises it sold. Purchasing real estate from such a company by an individual making a one-time payment of over RMB 100,000 is a major transaction, and the risk is naturally very high. Faced with a very risky transaction, Sun Haitao should have taken necessary precautionary measures. However, he did not take any precautions and did not request Xuanyu Company to issue a formal invoice, which is questionable. This is because temporary receipts may not be entered into accounts and are for temporary use, whereas formal invoices must be entered into accounts, are formal, and can be checked.

Sixth, more importantly, the receipt itself is full of loopholes. 1. The amounts in figures and words are inconsistent. The amount in figures is the contract amount "RMB 105,462", but the amount in words is "One Hundred and Five Thousand", with no "Four Hundred and Sixty-Two Yuan Only" following. As a person with full civil capacity, why did Sun Haitao not request Xuanyu Company to rewrite the receipt in light of this obvious inconsistency? 2. The columns for financial officer in charge, bookkeeper, cashier, reviewer, and handler are all blank. Why did none of the above personnel of the payee sign? In particular, the handler should have signed. Why did Sun Haitao not raise this issue? This is clearly inconsistent with the usual practice of the payee's staff in writing receipts. 3. The spaces before the year, month, and day of the date are all blank. This is also inconsistent with the usual practice of the payee's staff in writing receipts. 4. The official seal was not affixed at the "Unit Seal" location in the lower left corner, but rather in the middle-right part of the receipt.

Seventh, given that the receipt itself, by which Xuanyu Company acknowledged receipt of the payment, is full of loopholes, that this evidence is a single piece of evidence with no supporting accounting records, and that Xuanyu Company has an interest relationship with Hua Zhenming, this Court cannot be convinced that Xuanyu Company actually received the payment. According to Article 8 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, which provides that "during the litigation process, if one party clearly admits the facts of the case stated by the other party, the other party is exempted from the burden of proof, except for cases involving personal status relations," the effect of an admission applies only between the opposing parties in the litigation and cannot apply to a third party. In other words, a third party is not bound by such an admission. In this case, the plaintiff is Hua Zhenming, and the defendants are Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company. Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company are not opposing parties in this case; rather, their litigation objectives are consistent, namely, to prevent Hua Zhenming from enforcing against the disputed premises. Therefore, Xuanyu Company's admission that Sun Haitao paid the price for the premises has no binding force on Hua Zhenming. Consequently, with only Xuanyu Company's admission, unsupported by other evidence from Xuanyu Company such as accounting records, and given that the sole piece of evidence admitted is not a formal invoice but a receipt that is itself full of loopholes, this Court cannot be convinced that Xuanyu Company received the payment.

Eighth, because Sun Haitao's statement regarding Xuanyu Company's delivery of the keys is false, and because the receipt he presented, due to multiple aspects inconsistent with common experience of daily life, cannot form this Court's inner conviction that he had paid the price on March 2, 2006, the likelihood that his statement about paying the contract price is false is very high.

Pursuant to Article 64 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, and taking into comprehensive consideration the above eight factors, this Court determines that Sun Haitao did not deliver the premises price of RMB 105,462 to Xuanyu Company on March 2, 2006.

(II) As previously stated, at the time of the seizure on October 12, 2007, Sun Haitao did not occupy the disputed premises. Since he did not occupy them, he does not enjoy the so-called "priority of residence," especially since the premises are not for residential use. Moreover, since Sun Haitao did not pay the price for the premises before the seizure on October 12, 2007, his current possession of the disputed premises is not in good faith but constitutes possession in bad faith. This Court's determination is further corroborated by numerous pieces of evidence, such as Sun Haitao's statement that "payment was made first, then the contract was signed"; the fact that, in Sun Haitao's presence, his signature on the contract was executed by his wife; the absence of a date beneath Sun Haitao's signature at the end of the contract; many important contents of the contract being blank; the excessively long interval between the withdrawal date and the payment date; the receipt itself being full of loopholes; and the contradictions in Sun Haitao's statements regarding who was given the keys to the premises, among others.

In contrast, Hua Zhenming's application for seizure was made in good faith and is lawful. Hua Zhenming is a creditor of Xuanyu Company. When Xuanyu Company failed to voluntarily perform its debts, Hua Zhenming's application for seizure of the disputed premises, which belong to Xuanyu Company, and request for compulsory enforcement, complies with the law. When the people's court conducted the seizure, it found that no one was in possession of the premises. It is now also established that Sun Haitao did not deliver the price of the premises to Xuanyu Company before the seizure. Therefore, Hua Zhenming's seizure application is lawful, and the people's court's seizure is lawful. Consequently, Sun Haitao's possession in bad faith cannot oppose Hua Zhenming's seizure application and cannot oppose the people's court's compulsory enforcement. In other words, Hua Zhenming, as a creditor of Xuanyu Company, has the right to apply for seizure of the disputed premises and to request compulsory enforcement.

III. Regarding the consequences of Sun Haitao entering into a commodity housing sale contract with Xuanyu Company when Xuanyu Company did not have a pre-sale permit

It must be specifically pointed out that under circumstances where Xuanyu Company did not have a commodity housing pre-sale permit (and still does not to date), Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company entered into a commodity housing sale contract riddled with suspicions. Pursuant to Article 45, Paragraph 1, Item (4) of the Urban Real Estate Administration Law, which provides that for pre-sale of commodity housing, one "shall register for pre-sale with the real estate administration department of the people's government at or above the county level and obtain a commodity housing pre-sale permit," and pursuant to Article 2 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Disputes over Commodity Housing Sale Contracts, which provides that "a commodity housing pre-sale contract entered into between a seller and a buyer without the seller having obtained a commodity housing pre-sale permit shall be deemed invalid; however, if the seller obtains a commodity housing pre-sale permit before the lawsuit is filed, it may be deemed valid," this contract is invalid. Because an invalid contract is void ab initio and illegal, and the law imposes a negative evaluation on it, the contract between Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company is not protected by law, and the risks of this contract can only be borne by Sun Haitao himself. In other words, if Xuanyu Company had no debts, or voluntarily repaid its debts, the issue of its creditor applying to the people's court for compulsory enforcement would not arise, and the premises currently possessed by Sun Haitao would be safe and would not be subject to compulsory enforcement. However, once Xuanyu Company becomes involved in a dispute with its creditors, and in a situation like the present case, the premises currently occupied by Sun Haitao may also be denied legal protection. Therefore, strict compliance with the law by Sun Haitao is very important. Suppose Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company had complied with the law: if they had entered into the commodity housing sale contract only after Xuanyu Company obtained a commodity housing pre-sale permit, and then registered the contract for archival purposes, then at the time of seizure, the people's court would have been able to ascertain whether the property in question had been sold. If it had been sold, the people's court would then further examine whether Sun Haitao had paid part or all of the price, whether he actually occupied the property, and whether Sun Haitao was at fault for failing to complete the transfer registration, before deciding whether to proceed with the seizure. In that case, Sun Haitao's lawful rights and interests would have been protected. However, the actual situation is that both Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company failed to comply with the law. They entered into a commodity housing sale contract without Xuanyu Company having a pre-sale permit, rendering the contract incapable of being registered for archival purposes. Consequently, when the people's court seized the disputed premises, it could not ascertain whether the premises had already been sold by Xuanyu Company. The consequences of this must be borne solely by Sun Haitao and Xuanyu Company, and not by the applicant for the seizure, Hua Zhenming. It is evident that the root cause of this case lies in Sun Haitao's non-compliance with the law. For this, Sun Haitao himself cannot shirk responsibility. The outcome of losing the case is one he brought upon himself.

IV. Regarding whether there is evidence proving that the ownership of the premises belongs to Xuanyu Company and whether the courts of first and second instance confused legal relationships

In his application for retrial, Sun Haitao argued that the original judgment permitted enforcement but lacked evidence of the basic fact that the subject of enforcement actually belonged to the judgment debtor, Xuanyu Company. This argument is clearly untenable because the land use right for the land on which the disputed premises are situated belongs to Xuanyu Company, and the disputed premises are not registered in anyone else's name. According to the general principle for determining property ownership that "the building follows the land," the ownership of the premises should be considered to belong to Xuanyu Company.

In his retrial application, Sun Haitao also argued that the original judgment confused legal relationships. He claimed that the court of first instance examined the preservation measure, while the court of second instance focused its adjudication on whether Sun Haitao had acquired the property in good faith, and that neither court examined whether Hua Zhenming had a right that could oppose Sun Haitao's right or whether enforcement could continue. This argument cannot stand. The court of first instance held that "Hua Zhenming's claim against Xuanyu Company, as confirmed by effective judgment documents of the people's court, is lawful and valid. Since Xuanyu Company is unable to perform the repayment obligation determined in the judgment, the creditor Hua Zhenming's application to enforce Xuanyu Company's real property to satisfy the debt also complies with the law. The evidence submitted by the defendant Sun Haitao in this case is insufficient to prove that the commodity housing sale contract between him and Xuanyu Company had been actually performed at the time this court seized the disputed premises, nor can it prove that he had actually occupied the disputed premises at the time of this court's seizure. His claim that Xuanyu Company had delivered the disputed premises and keys to him for use on March 2, 2006 is not supported by sufficient evidence and is thus not upheld by this court." The two reasons stated above by the court of first instance serve to demonstrate that Hua Zhenming had the right to seize the disputed premises and apply for compulsory enforcement, and the result indicates that Hua Zhenming's right can oppose Sun Haitao's right. The court of second instance held that "Sun Haitao purchased the property in dispute in this case when Xuanyu Company had not obtained a commodity housing pre-sale permit, and he failed to provide a formal invoice for the purchase of the property to the court. As a person with full civil capacity, when purchasing a commodity of significant value such as a house, he did not exercise the corresponding duty of care. The act of buying and selling the house between the parties involves significant defects. Moreover, the evidence submitted by Sun Haitao during the first and second instance trials was insufficient to prove that he actually occupied the property in dispute. His claim of simultaneously purchasing multiple sets of houses does not lead to his enjoyment of related rights in the property in dispute in this case. Therefore, the evidence provided by Sun Haitao does not prove that he enjoys the substantive rights sufficient to prevent the transfer or delivery of the property in dispute in this case. Sun Haitao's claims on appeal lack sufficient evidence and are not supported by this court." From the reasoning of the court of second instance, it is clear that its analysis sought to demonstrate that Hua Zhenming's right could oppose Sun Haitao's right, and that Hua Zhenming had the right to seize the disputed premises and apply for compulsory enforcement. Therefore, this ground for retrial raised by Sun Haitao cannot be established.

In conclusion, Sun Haitao's grounds for retrial application do not satisfy the circumstances provided in Items (2) and (6) of Article 200 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 204, Paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

Sun Haitao's application for retrial is rejected.
